tasks.title: Reconciliation data in the cell model
tasks.detail: Every cell can carry a Recon: id, service, identifierSpace, schemaSpace, judgment (none / matched / new), judgmentAction, judgmentHistoryEntry, match (id, name, types, score), candidates (ranked), features (typeMatch, nameMatch, nameLevenshtein, nameWordDistance), matchRank. Stored beside the dictionary codes, not in them. GREL sees cell.recon.* (judgment, match, best, candidates, features, service…). Recon data reads from and writes to OpenRefine project archives (the recon pool in data.txt and change files) instead of being dropped, and survives operations that move cells (column copy, move, reorder, rows remove/reorder, fill down/blank down, records).

tasks.title: Reconciliation API client and the reconcile operation
tasks.detail: W3C Reconciliation API client: fetch a service manifest, batched queries (OpenRefine's batch size), type constraint, property constraints from other columns, limit, auto-match (OpenRefine's rule: top candidate matched when its score and the gap to the second qualify). The core/recon operation with StandardReconConfig JSON, same output cells as OpenRefine; long-running job with progress and cancel. Service list kept in preferences, with Wikidata as a preset; 'guess types of column'. The reconcile dialog: service, type, columns as properties, auto-match toggle. Tests run against a local mock service with fixtures from OpenRefine 3.10.1.

tasks.title: Matching UI

Backed by recon-judge-one-cell and recon-judge-similar-cells, with the same history entries. (Searching with the suggest API and the preview flyout: rc-suggest.)

tasks.title: Reconciliation facets

Same facet JSON in engineConfig, so recipes with these facets replay.

tasks.title: Benchmark tracking
tasks.detail: Run the comparison on every release and publish the chart, and catch regressions: on Nov 11 a hand check against the first prototype found the list facet 6x slower (per-row string keys), peak RAM up 70% from saving (a JSON tree of the whole table) and export (the whole CSV in memory). Keep a baseline results.json, an OxRefine-only fast mode for CI, and fail on per-step slowdowns and memory growth beyond noise.

tasks.title: Import memory
tasks.detail: After the Nov 11 fixes peak RAM at 1M rows is 141 MB against the prototype's 122; the remainder is probably the parallel import's batches and per-worker dictionaries. Measure per step, trim without losing the 4x import speed-up.
